title: Authorize narrowly scoped cross-account publication inference
description:
Feature: Owner-authorized cross-account inference
Scenario: Explicit owner delegation
Given distinct synthetic owner and consumer SaaS accounts and an owner-approved grant for one bound publication output
When a freshly authenticated consumer requests inference
Then the same owner engine executes under its exact execution binding
And only allowed results and content-free attribution are disclosed
And owner policies, labels, sources, feedback and administration remain inaccessible
Scenario: Authority changes
Given queued or completed inference
When the grant expires, is revoked, changes revision or fresh authorization fails
Then execution or disclosure is refused without retrying uncertain provider work
Scenario: Separate internal router
Given an allowed central publication match
When handed to a consumer-owned internal section router
Then tenant, source revision, central decision and publication provenance are retained
And no section label or feedback is invented.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Claim: separate clone cyclotron-sharing at origin/develop 38ea51d. Only new publication_sharing.py and adjacent specs plus docs/publication-sharing.md. Central monitoring owner notified with exact files; existing PR58/runtime/auth/queue/publication_lab paths remain unmodified. Claude route requested from owner. Synthetic contract enforcement is independent of four-output priming; hosted integration tracked separately. Domain and criteria expected later today; no repeated request. Current core computes all central outputs, so execution scope must be distinct from visible scope; display usage estimates are not billing authority.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Acceptance refinement from independent review: besides delegated inference, central publication fan-out must deliver an already-computed decision to an explicitly addressed consumer/publication with the original source account/revision and central decision identity. Delivery performs no provider call and exposes only the granted output. A guessed owner receipt ID cannot confer access to arbitrary owner sources/history. Revalidate recipient authority, grant revision, execution binding and exact addressed delivery before disclosure. Synthetic tests must prove one central decision can reach the separate internal section router without a duplicate classification or copied feedback. Runtime activation remains separate.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Implemented an additive, transport-independent owner-grant contract in publication_sharing.py and adjacent synthetic specifications. Explicit operation scope separates delegated inference from addressed delivery of an existing central decision. Delivery does not call the model again; consumers receive only approved outputs. Native account/list/item/integer revision/hash provenance, nullable origin publication, owner billing attribution, revocation, expiry, caller-bound retries, atomic store/audit ports and source-validation boundaries are preserved.

Final root verification: 118 sharing specifications pass. The author also passed 50 existing account/publication regressions (168 total); root independently passed 57 neighboring regressions earlier. Ruff, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent review found no remaining blocking findings in this source-only scope. An actual native offline Cyclotron decision passed through the generated sharing receipt into the Papyrus handoff: two outputs computed, one disclosed, one original model call, zero extra delivery/section calls; stable retry and revocation checked.

This is source groundwork, not a deployed sharing service. Durable production store/current authority/catalog/native adapters and authenticated receipt transport remain tracked by decision-flywheel-e523bb3e-1b19-41dc-97d9-ae367ca36174. No grants, credentials, security expansion, production model calls or runtime/worker edits occurred. Original four-output priming remains independent.
